method: Screened quantitative medieval island and North Atlantic records for the evidence contract. Fiscal enumerations and market records are not treated as intrinsic carrying-capacity labels unless the same boundary has an independently measured local-food ceiling and dated pressure evidence. Candidates that fail remain explicit rejections or validation-only observations.

promotion_audit.decision: No new training anchor passes. Mallorca has a valuable 1329 fiscal population reconstruction but documented wheat-import dependence and a wealth-biased morabeti assessment; it is not an upper local-food capacity. Crete has grain-market and purchase records but no same-boundary population/capacity interval and strong Venetian market dependence. Sardinia has qualitative late-medieval underpopulation and subsistence-crisis evidence without an auditable dated population/capacity interval. North Orkney, Shetland, and the Faroes document settlement, pasture and marine-food systems but not a 1290-1337 human equilibrium interval. Keep these as rejected or held-out validation candidates; do not lower the promotion threshold.

records.boundary_status: historical_island_boundary described; EU5 selector/crosswalk not yet audited
records.capacity_status: no intrinsic upper capacity; morabeti is a fiscal wealth/eligibility record
records.pressure_status: fertile districts and intensive agriculture documented; famine/epidemic shocks and post-1329 decline documented, but no dated saturation fraction
records.local_food_status: fails local-food criterion for an upper target: medieval Mallorca had recurrent wheat deficits and documented imports
records.reason: The 1329 morabeti reconstruction gives approximately 59,620 taxable persons, with estimates around 63,000 to 70,000 after accounting for non-payers. The assessment began in 1266 and was collected from heads of households above a wealth threshold, so it is not a complete headcount. Mallorca also imported wheat and used regulated grain shipping to cover shortages; observed population therefore cannot cap locally supportable people. Retain only as a validation population floor after a boundary crosswalk is built.
sources: https://publicacions.iec.cat/repository/pdf/00000158/00000049.pdf (Santamaria, Demografia de Mallorca, 1329 morabeti discussion, pp. 155-222)
https://www.mdpi.com/2071-1050/11/1/168 (Mallorca agrarian intensity and demographic decline after 1329)

records.boundary_status: historical island boundary described; EU5 selector/crosswalk not audited
records.capacity_status: no aggregate population or local-food capacity interval
records.pressure_status: grain-price volatility and market procurement are documented; they do not identify a local equilibrium ceiling
records.local_food_status: mixed and unresolved; Venetian procurement and inter-territorial grain circulation are material
records.reason: The 1300-1330 records provide grain prices and a Venetian purchase contract for roughly 100,000 mouzouria from Chania producers, but no contemporaneous aggregate population or land/calorie ceiling for the island. Market procurement, port redistribution and price observations cannot supervise surrounding intrinsic capacity. Retain as a qualitative irrigation/grain-market validation case only.
sources: https://www.mdpi.com/1911-8074/14/4/151 (Crete grain prices and 1330 Chania purchase)

records.boundary_status: exact island area benchmark available; historical sub-boundary and population crosswalk absent
records.pressure_status: qualitative evidence of exhausted holdings, abandoned land, debt, high grain prices and recurrent subsistence crises
records.local_food_status: rural pastoral, hunting, fishing and gathering systems documented; aggregate local-calorie share is not quantified
records.reason: Day's Annales study directly discusses late-medieval Sardinian underpopulation and subsistence calamities, but the accessible record does not provide a mappable 1290-1337 population interval or an independently estimated carrying-capacity ceiling for the same boundary. The exact island area benchmark is therefore useful for model stress testing only; no numeric target is fabricated.
sources: https://doi.org/10.3406/ahess.1975.293640 (John Day, Malthus démenti? Sous-peuplement chronique et calamités démographiques en Sardaigne au bas Moyen Âge)

records.boundary_status: six-island study boundary is explicit but EU5 crosswalk not audited
records.pressure_status: archaeological settlement and farm/fishing continuity; no dated saturation interval
records.local_food_status: mixed farming, fishing and fish processing documented, but calories are not aggregated
records.reason: The North Orkney Population History Project documents continuous Norse-era settlement and archaeological farms/fishing, while modern population peaked at 6,062 in 1861. It supplies no defensible 1290-1337 population interval or local-food capacity ceiling. Keep as a future hostile-island validation candidate, not a target.

records.boundary_status: island geography described; EU5 crosswalk not audited
records.capacity_status: carrying-capacity dissertation is Iron Age and out of target period
records.pressure_status: pasture and marine productivity modeled, but not 1290-1337
records.local_food_status: ecological potential only; no medieval calorie balance
records.reason: The available quantitative Shetland carrying-capacity work is an Iron Age ecological study. Its date and technology do not match 1337, so it cannot train the 1337 model. Retain only as an out-of-period physical validation analogue pending a medieval boundary-specific record.
